claim: Under GWT, the brain has many parallel specialist processors and one limited-capacity workspace; the selected item is broadcast to all, and effortful or novel tasks need it while routine ones do not.
agent_test: Compare an agent that sees all candidate thoughts versus one where code selects a single item and broadcasts only it, at equal tokens.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-10 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Conscious access shows a nonlinear, all-or-none threshold: visibility ratings are bimodal and a late (about 250-300 ms) component bifurcates seen from unseen while early sensory activity is preserved.
agent_test: Analogy only: test whether a hard commit step (accept or reject a candidate) beats soft weighting of candidates.

claim: P3b is not a necessary marker of access: it disappears when stimuli are task-irrelevant; VAN/N2 in 200-300 ms persists. Late ignition may reflect report, not experience.
agent_test: None direct; warns against treating 'late sustained activity' as proof of a workspace.

claim: Cogitate adversarial test (N=256) challenged GNWT: no offset ignition in PFC (0 of 655 electrodes with onset+offset profile), orientation not decodable in PFC; preregistered connectivity analysis supported neither theory; category decodable in PFC only briefly (iEEG about 70% vs posterior over 95%). Published Nature text re-read.
agent_test: None; theory status matters only for how strongly we cite GWT as justification.

claim: Resolved: the published Nature text (PMC12137136) reports category decodable in PFC but adding PFC to posterior decoders gave no gain (iEEG BF01 1.94e4 and 1.91e5; MEG 3.05 and 4.70). The preprint reading that category decoding supports GNWT is superseded. Prediction 3 (connectivity): preregistered result supported neither theory (iEEG BF01 2.62 to 5.32).
agent_test: None. Use only as a caution: PFC carries abstract category, not fine detail.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-10 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: GNWT and its critics disagree about what the data mean: GNWT camp says no visible/invisible contrast was run so the core contrast was untested; decoding in cortex also works for non-conscious stimuli.
agent_test: None.

claim: A small shared workspace (few slots, write by competition, read by broadcast) in neural nets gives modest gains over pairwise attention at lower cost; gains on CATER are within noise (71.07 vs 70.83, SD 0.44).
agent_test: Cap the shared scratchpad at k items and compare to unrestricted context at equal tokens.

claim: Slot count matters nonmonotonically: bouncing balls ARI 0.154 (2 slots), 0.487 (4), 0.915 (5), 0.891 (8), 0.351 (10), baseline 0.276. Too narrow or too wide bottleneck both hurt (one task, one paper, confirmed against PDF).
agent_test: Sweep workspace size (e.g. 3, 5, 8, 12 items) on one fixed task set; expect an interior optimum.

claim: A GW agent beat a GRU in audiovisual navigation (about 80% vs just over 60%, read from figures) with no benefit from larger workspaces; probes lost target info once sound stopped. Authors say SAVi is not an adequate working-memory benchmark. No replication found (re-opened full text).
agent_test: Test whether a broadcast summary helps most when context budget is small.

claim: Semi-supervised GW translation needed 4-7x less paired data (6x on Simple Shapes: N=5,000 matches N=30,000; 4.5x on captions); ImageNet probe 55.7 +/- 0.2% vs 50.3 +/- 0.2% contrastive-only. Re-opened and confirmed; gain mostly from cycle-consistency with unpaired data. Only extension by the same group (Maytie 2024), no independent replication.
agent_test: None (representation learning, not reasoning).

claim: Butlin et al. translate GWT into four AI indicators (parallel modules, limited-capacity workspace, global broadcast, state-dependent attention). Plain Transformers and the residual stream fail; Perceiver partly meets GWT-2 and GWT-4. Language agents are arguably closer.
agent_test: Check our scaffold against the four indicators as a design checklist.

claim: Generative-agent architecture (memory stream, retrieval picks few memories, reflection, planning) beat ablations on believability: TrueSkill 29.89 full vs 26.88 no reflection vs 21.21 none (100 raters). Confirmed against the PDF.
agent_test: Ablate retrieval selection and reflection in our agent; measure at equal tokens.

claim: The workspace is tied to System-2 style controlled processing: it holds a goal and interim conclusions and passes queries between modules.
agent_test: Test explicit running summary of interim conclusions versus raw history.

claim: Anthropic 'J-space' paper is real (transformer-circuits.pub, 6 July 2026; OpenAlex arXiv 2607.15495): capacity at most 25 J-lens vectors, never above 10% of activation variance; causal swaps 54/70/70% (Haiku/Sonnet/Opus 4.5, 50 prompts), top-1% broadcast-head ablation drops recall@25 0.86 to 0.67 and injected-thought report 0.54 to 0.09; reflection fine-tuning lowers fabrication 0.25 to 0.07 and deception 0.38 to 0.05. Numbers verified against page text. Vendor's own work, not independently replicated, single-token lens only.
agent_test: Treat as a measurement that a few items carry verbalizable content, not as proof that a scaffold helps. Cite with the single-vendor caveat.

claim: Proposed 'Global Workspace Agents' for LLMs (cognitive tick, critic scores -5 to +5, entropy-driven temperature) have no experiments.
agent_test: Implement tick loop in a minimal form and measure against a plain loop.

claim: No study found that tests a workspace bottleneck (k-item shared scratchpad, one item broadcast) on LLM reasoning accuracy at equal tokens. Closest: MemAgent (1,024-token overwrite memory, RL-trained, retrieval QA), context curation (WebArena 36.4 to 41.2% with 8.8% fewer tokens), Tree of Thoughts keep-and-prune (74% vs CoT best-of-100 49% at about equal tokens), and BIGMAS (GWT-framed, 2 to 6 point gains, N=100, not token-matched). Searched 2023-2026 across OpenAlex, arXiv pages and web.
agent_test: This is the key untested question for our agent.

claim: Context length itself hurts: with perfect retrieval, accuracy dropped 13.9% to 85% as input grew in 5 LLMs, even with irrelevant tokens masked; reciting the evidence first gave up to 4% on RULER. Supports carrying forward a short curated item rather than all candidates.
agent_test: Compare an agent that carries one chosen item with one that carries all candidate thoughts, at matched total tokens.

claim: Constant-size working memory with forced overwrite works for LLMs: MemAgent (1,024-token memory, 8K window) reports under 5% loss out to 3.5M tokens and over 95% at 512K RULER; memory length 256 to 4,096 was robust with 1,024 a sweet spot. RL-trained and retrieval-heavy, so a weak analogy for prompt-only reasoning.
agent_test: Cap carried state at a fixed token budget and rewrite it each step; measure accuracy against an uncapped log.

claim: In a blackboard multi-agent LLM system, a control unit that chooses who acts and a cleaner that deletes stale messages cut tokens about 3x (MMLU 5.07M vs 18.83M) with accuracy within noise (85.17 vs 85.52); marking redundant messages instead of deleting them lowered accuracy (MMLU 84.38, MATH 71.00). A second blackboard system beat RAG and master-slave on KramaBench-type tasks at about 2.3x and 1.8x cost. Selection saves cost, not accuracy.
agent_test: Ablate selection and deletion of stale items in our agent; expect a token saving, test for any accuracy change.

claim: Keep-few-and-prune search beat unstructured sampling at about equal tokens: Game of 24 ToT b=5 74% vs CoT best-of-100 49% at 5.5k vs 6.7k tokens; b=1 gave 45%; crossword without pruning was worse and without backtracking 20% word-level. This supports hard selection of a few candidates but does not isolate a single committed item vs soft mixing.
agent_test: Run keep-1 hard commit vs keep-5 vs soft merge on the same budget.

claim: No evidence found for an interior optimum of workspace size in LLM agents. Goyal's non-monotone slot curve (small net) has no LLM replication; Dossa found flat performance across memory sizes 32 to 512; MemAgent memory length 256 to 4,096 was robust; the blackboard round sweep is noisy (GPQA 52.0, 54.0, 53.0, 51.0 at 2/4/6/8 rounds); Phua's toy shows a threshold at zero slots, not a peak.
agent_test: Sweep carried-item count k in our agent; do not assume a peak.

claim: Only a few LLM systems carry a GWT label with benchmark numbers: BIGMAS (Game 24 25 to 36, Six Fives 12 to 30, Tower of London 6 to 20 on DeepSeek-V3.2, N=100) and CogniPair (72% correlation, 77.8% match accuracy). Neither tests the workspace against a no-workspace control at equal tokens. A practitioner memory runtime (gwt-context) states it proves no reasoning gains. Theater of Mind (c14) remains unevaluated; Tait 2026 could not be opened.
agent_test: Treat GWT labels in agent papers as marketing until a matched-token ablation exists.

claim: 2026 meta-analysis (117 studies, Psych Bulletin): VAN SMD 0.37 [0.32, 0.43], P3b 0.49 [0.41, 0.57]; P3b absent when task-irrelevant (-0.12 [-0.47, 0.23]); VAN present without awareness. Headline numbers confirmed from the abstract; full text and moderators not seen.
agent_test: Do not use late sustained activity as proof of a workspace.
